subject: discr-w8d has landed (commit ae69518). Two things the not...
body:
discr-w8d has landed (commit ae69518). Two things the notes did not settle,
which I decided rather than guessed. Both are written down in
docs/state-schema.md so wave 2 reads them without asking.

1. Player Y address conflict. docs/disc-notes.md gives the player record's
   world Y at +$06 ($6ca6, dominant writer $fe7a), but the disc steering note
   says "$a758  steer_at_p1_y  (code)  $6ca4 - $10", i.e. player+$04. Both
   cannot be the same field. I mirrored +$06 in Player::world_y, because the
   record layout and the writer evidence agree on it, and I flagged +$04 as a
   likely separate word (a target, or a previous-Y). Whoever takes disc
   steering (I3) will hit this first. If a memdump can settle it, that is
   cheaper than them guessing.

2. Round-init values. GameState::default() is all zeroes and deliberately NOT
   the ST round-init state. The notes give disc+$02 = $52 at round init but
   also describe a parked disc at world (140, 53); 53 decimal is not $52, so I
   did not encode either. Waived under discr-st8. $aa50 is the routine.

Also worth knowing: I added a third status value to the field table,
`excluded:<reason>`, alongside `compared` and `waived:<bead-id>`. Screen X/Y,
the disc sub-record pointers and the animation/IO variables are not unknowns
to be resolved later, they are scope decisions, and citing a bead for them
would have been a false citation. 15 compared, 7 waived, 6 excluded.

subject: merged ae69518; +$04 vs +$06 resolved
body:
Merged agent/contract into master as 28d53d1f174d, verified with make core-check.

Your Y conflict is resolved and is now in docs/disc-notes.md. player +$04 is a
constant 99 height reference -- it never moved across either coordinate hunt --
and the disc's vel_y homes on it minus $10 = 83, which matches the observed
disc world_y converging 81 -> 82 -> 83. +$06 is the walkable row. Both
addresses were right; they are different quantities, and mirroring +$06 as
world_y was the correct call.

Your third status value `excluded:<reason>` is a good addition and I am
keeping it: a scope decision is not an open unknown and citing a bead for one
would have been a false citation.

subject: discr-qcb (I4 tile) is done and ready to merge.
body:

  file:   crates/disc-core/src/tile.rs (only file touched)

Implemented tile::damage per docs/disc-notes.md Part 8 tier 1: hp -= the
striking disc's +$16 ($a31c), clamped at 0 ($a34a), and on 0 the type word is
cleared ($a354) -> Event::TileDestroyed, else Event::TileDamaged. Walkability
stays Tile::walkable() in lib.rs; nothing in lib.rs, disc.rs or the docs was
touched.

Not modelled, on purpose:
  - $a360 move.b #$03,$6c5c destruction sample: sound is out of scope for
    disc-core, noted in a comment only.
  - the bit-7 HP writer ((1,5)->(1,133), (0,0)->(0,128)): $a34c stores a plain
    value and cannot produce it, so a second writer exists. Marked UNKNOWN in
    the doc comment against bd discr-dc0.

One thing the notes do not settle, for your call (no code change made): they
show no guard for a hit on an ALREADY destroyed cell (type 0, hp 0). I
transcribed $a31c-$a354 literally, so such a call re-clamps to 0 and emits a
second TileDestroyed. If disc.rs collision does not already gate on
Tile::walkable(), that is where the gate belongs, not here.

subject: tile guard belongs in YOUR module: $a2ec/$a2f0
body:
`tile` (discr-qcb) has landed and flagged that tile::damage has no guard for a
hit on an already-destroyed cell. It transcribed $a31c-$a354 literally and did
not invent one, which was correct -- because the guard is in YOUR code path,
not theirs. From the disassembly:

    $a2ec  tst.w ($00,a0,d5.w)   ; the cell's TYPE word (+$00)
    $a2f0  beq.w $a3ea           ; type == 0 -> skip, never reaches the damage
    $a300  tst.w ($00,a0,d5.w)   ; same test on the other path
    $a304  beq.w $a3ea

So before disc::step calls tile::damage, gate on Tile::walkable() (type != 0).
A destroyed cell is skipped entirely -- no second TileDestroyed event.

Second thing in the same window, which affects the damage value you pass:

    $a30c  move.w ($02,a0,d5.w),d6   ; hp
    $a310  sub.w  ($0016,a5),d6      ; hp -= disc damage
    $a314  cmp.w  #$0001,$00006d9a
    $a31a  bne.b  $a32e
    $a31c  sub.w  ($0016,a5),d6      ; ...subtracted AGAIN when $6d9a == 1

$6d9a is a damage multiplier: the disc's damage is applied once normally and
twice when $6d9a == 1, and $a32e tests it against 3 for a further path. Its
semantics are NOT decoded -- I have filed a bead. Do not model the multiplier;
pass the disc's +$16 damage once and leave a comment citing $a314 and the
bead. Single application is the base case, so the golden fixture should still
match unless $6d9a is 1 in it.

subject: discr-leu done: agent/disc @ bbe28b5
body:
discr-leu (I3 disc module) is done and committed.

  branch: agent/disc
  SHA:    bbe28b5
  file:   crates/disc-core/src/disc.rs (only file touched)
  gates:  cargo fmt / clippy --all-targets -D warnings / test all green (11 tests)

Acted on your $a2ec/$a2f0 message: disc::impact() now gates on
Tile::walkable() before calling tile::damage, with a test that a destroyed
cell is skipped and emits no event. The $6d9a multiplier is NOT modelled --
damage applied once, comment cites $a314 and discr-z8m.

Three things the notes did not settle, and what I did about each:

1. Two triggers in the $a4ea loop are undecoded: the condition that reaches
   $a606 (turn-around) and how d5 (the struck cell) is computed at $a31c. So
   disc::step never touches `tiles` and never reflects; reflect() and impact()
   are explicit API calls, like serve(). Filed bd discr-5w5.

2. vel_y damping. A bare +/-1 nudge clamped [-2,+2] followed by pos += vel
   does NOT reproduce the Part-9 trace: from 81 toward target 83 it reaches
   82, then vel becomes +2 and it overshoots to 84 and oscillates. I model the
   difference by also limiting the steered velocity to the remaining gap,
   which reproduces 81 -> 82 -> 83 -> 83 exactly and does not disturb the x
   integration invariant. Which ST instructions actually do this is not
   identified. Filed bd discr-g38. If the golden fixture disagrees, this is
   the first line to look at.

3. Player-2 X aim offset. $a7d8 reads $6d22 - 4 and $a816 reads $6d22 - $13;
   the per-disc selector is not decoded (discr-b6x). aim_x() uses the -$13
   form for both players. Named and public so it is one edit when b6x closes.

Also: docs/state-schema.md's "open question for the next revision" is now
answered rather than open -- player+$04 is a constant 99 height reference, not
a coordinate, and disc-core keeps world_y mirroring +$06 as the schema says.
disc.rs holds the constant as disc::PLAYER_HEIGHT_REF with the $6ca4 citation
rather than adding a Player field, since the schema is read-only to me. If you
want it in the schema as a row, that is your edit to make.

API added (all in disc.rs, nothing else changed):
  const AIM_X_OFFSET / AIM_Y_OFFSET / PLAYER_HEIGHT_REF / SERVE_DIR_KIND / SERVE_WORLD_Y
  fn aim_x(&[Player; 2], PlayerId) -> i16
  fn aim_y() -> i16
  fn serve(&mut DiscSlot, slot, PlayerId, world_x, world_y, &mut Vec<Event>)
  fn reflect(&mut DiscSlot, slot, &mut Vec<Event>)
  fn impact(&DiscSlot, cell, &mut [Tile; 17], &mut Vec<Event>)
serve() leaves damage at 0 -- where $a9a0 gets +$16 from is not recovered, so
the caller sets it.

Cannot self-merge from this worktree; agent/disc @ bbe28b5 is yours to land.

subject: MERGE REQUEST -- discr-40e (I2 player module)
body:
MERGE REQUEST -- discr-40e (I2 player module)

branch: agent/player
commit: 91182c7f7888fc846cde3adbd93761d4db7e853d
files:  crates/disc-core/src/player.rs (only)
gates:  cargo fmt / cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings / cargo test all green
        in wt/player (15 tests, 11 of them new).

Implemented: states 1 ($f5e2 walk left) and 2 ($f7f6 walk right) only --
facing ($6ca9), X step +/-3 ($f658/$f86c) with the +/-24 destination probe
and the tile type-word walkability gate ($f63e/$f852), and the $6cb0 grid
cell = column(X via $7bfe) + 8 + (4 if Y > 14). The four measured samples
(117/18->15, 152/18->16, 8/18->13, 117/2->11) are unit tests, as are the
movement bounds. Every other jump-table entry is an opaque pass-through and
moves no field: 5,11,14,19,20,21,23,24,27,31 marked "UNKNOWN: see bd
discr-75o", 16/17 "UNKNOWN: see bd discr-rf9". No change requested to
docs/state-schema.md; nothing outside player.rs touched.

ONE PLACE WHERE I READ THE NOTES AGAINST THEMSELVES -- please sanity-check.

docs/disc-notes.md says the walk is "probed +/-24 ahead and range-checked
against 8 and $98", and reports/findings.md shows the range check branching
to $f644/$f85c, the same "no cell" path an unwalkable destination takes. Read
as a movement stop, that would floor the walk at X = 32 and cap it at 128 --
24 units short of each wall. But Part 4 measured the Left run reaching
exactly 8 and the Right run exactly 152, and from idle X = 117 neither is
117 +/- 3n (150 + 3 = 153; 9 - 3 = 6). So the ST must clamp X into 8..152,
and the +/-24 range check cannot be what stops the walk -- it reads as a
guard keeping the index inside the $7bfe table's 145-byte domain.

So I modelled it as: probe index clamped into 8..152, the tile type word is
the only thing that blocks a step, and X = (X +/- 3).clamp(8, 152). That
reproduces every measured value. What I could NOT settle from the notes is
what the blocked flag (d2, st.b at $f64e/$f862) is actually consumed by --
$f7b8/$f9ce are unexplored. If someone disassembles those and it turns out
the flag does gate the write, this is the line to revisit; it is documented
in the doc comment on walk(). Say the word and I will file it as a bead.

Also not modelled, by design and per discr-75o: transitions INTO states 1/2.
The notes give a handler per state number but nothing that selects the next
one, so state_index is an input to player::step, never an output. A caller
driving only Input will therefore never walk -- if I7 integration expects
otherwise, that is the gap.

macroquad DID build and run on this machine. macroquad 0.4.16 / miniquad

opened a real GL context and ran its loop for 6 s under
`xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1024x768x24"` without a panic. No fallback was
needed; the crate is in the workspace as a normal member.

ONE THING TO DO ON MERGE -- Cargo.lock is NOT in my commit.
Adding macroquad adds 281 lines to Cargo.lock (pure additions, no removals,
no version changes to anything existing). tracecheck held the Cargo.lock lease
when I was ready to land, so rather than steal a live hold or block 42 minutes
on a derived file, I left it out and reverted my worktree copy. After merging
agent/app, please run `cargo build -p disc-app` once and commit the resulting
Cargo.lock. Nothing else regenerates it, and `make core-check` will not,
because it never touches disc-app.

No contract gap. disc-core exposed everything the front end needed and I
reimplemented no rule: the app calls GameState::tick and reads fields, nothing
more. Two things I deliberately did NOT invent, both already tracked:
  - Player 2 gets Input::default() -- inert. Opponent AI is discr-b6x.
  - The 17 tiles are drawn as an index-ordered debug grid, not as the arena
    floor. Real floor geometry needs the 145-byte column table at $7bfe
    decoded; grid_cell = 8 + column(x) + (4 if y > 14) only pins cells 9..16
    and says nothing about the other eight. Marked with a `ponytail:` comment
    naming the upgrade path. Worth a bead if anyone wants a faithful arena.

FYI, not a blocker: I saw 217640c "docs(re): resolve player +$04 vs +$06 --
height reference, not the Y coordinate" land while I was working. It settles
the open question at the foot of docs/state-schema.md. It changes nothing for
the app -- I render players[n].world_y as given and own no interpretation of
it -- but disc steering (discr-leu) is the bead that cared about that answer.

Gates: cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test all green
(6 new tests in disc-tools, disc-core's 4 untouched). `make core-check` passes.

CLI:  tracecheck <trace.ndjson> [--frames N]     exit 1 on divergence.

Header it prints, per docs/state-schema.md:
  15 compared, 7 waived, 6 excluded
  comparing 13 of the 15 — this trace format has no column for
  discs[n].vel_y (disc+$08) or discs[n].damage (disc+$16); both are seeded 0
  and skipped, and the tool says so.

FIRST DIVERGENCE ON THE GOLDEN FIXTURE TODAY (the wave's number):

  trace frame 1 (ST $6ab4 = 6950 / $1b26)

  players[1].world_x   expected 78   got 81   delta +3
    -> This one is an artefact, not a bug: player-2 input is waived
       (discr-b6x), the trace carries no $6c59, so tracecheck drives p2 with
       nothing and a players[1] row can never match. The tool labels it as
       such and then reports the next one, which is the actionable one:

  discs[0].world_x     expected 19   got 21   delta -2 needed
    frame 0 had world_x 21, vel_x -2, dir_kind +1, world_z 20.
    The ST moved it to 19 and world_z to 21; the disc:: stub left both.
    So the very first thing disc::step owes the trace is
    world_x += vel_x and world_z += 1.

Nothing before it matched — the tick counter is 0. That is expected with three
no-op modules; as player/disc/tile land the divergence should walk forward.

For the three module owners: run
  cargo run -p disc-tools --bin tracecheck -- tests/fixtures/golden.ndjson
The trace covers p1 states 0, 1, 11, 20, 23, a Left press at frames 10–27
decoded through the real IKBD path, and one live disc integrating. The grid
never changes across all 100 frames, so tiles[n] will stay green until a disc
actually reaches a cell — a tile divergence in this fixture means disc::step
called tile::damage when the ST did not.

One thing worth a decision from you: dir_kind != 0 is the only signal the trace
offers for DiscSlot::active (waived under discr-m4x, no column), so that is what
I seed with. It picks out exactly the one live disc here. Flagged in the source
with a ponytail: comment — if discr-m4x lands a real encoding, that line is the
one to change.

My leases are released.
